activities.name: f1000CoveragePlot

activities.anchor: Together they carry the sentence skeleton
activities.caption: file the first thousand by role
activities.name: f1000AnatomyBuckets

config.prompt: The anatomy of a first-1,000 list — file each layer:
buckets: the frame every sentence hangs on

items.label: function words: the, of, and, but, this, that
high-frequency verbs: be, have, go, want, can, make, say
a shell of concrete nouns and adjectives: water, house, mother, big, good

config.why: About twenty words run the CEFR's entire self-introduction can-do — twenty words, one descriptor.

activities.anchor: gender is free at first meeting and agonising
activities.caption: pair each bundling rule with its catch
activities.name: f1000BundleMatch

config.prompt: Two bundling rules multiply the yield — pair the practice with what it prevents:

pairs.left: carry plural types with the noun
pairs.right: no retrofitting grammatical baggage across a thousand words later
no "go + ed" reconstructed after the damage

pairs.left: record the word's common company ("make a decision")

pairs.right: one card encoding meaning, grammar and usage at once

config.why: Cards that carry a word plus its article plus one authentic sentence cost little extra — frequency dictionaries and corpora publish the company the word keeps.

config.q: Two beginners start today. One follows textbook chapters (animals, colours, classroom objects); one follows word counts. A month in, who can run a conversation?
choices: The chapter learner — grammar-first builds the foundations
The count learner — a few hundred words do most of the talking, and the little words smuggle grammar along for free
Neither — one month is too early for anyone
config.why: Chapter order spends the early budget on rare words; the other order spends it where the payoff is.

config.text: Spaced repetition schedules each card's next review just before you would likely %%forget%% it, and %%stretches%% the interval each time you succeed — one day, three days, a week, two weeks, a month.
config.hint: Both verbs are what the software does at the edge of the curve.

config.prompt: Sustained vocabulary growth tops out at roughly how many new words a day for a busy adult?
config.why: Ten to twenty — and some fraction fades anyway, which is why spending that budget on high-frequency words is the only rational allocation.
config.context: Dosage beats intensity: twenty minutes daily beats three hours weekly by an amount that surprises everyone who measures it.

activities.anchor: bad card design quietly kills more
activities.caption: find the line that kills decks
activities.name: f1000CardSpot

config.prompt: One line of these deck rules is the project-killer — click it:
lines: One fact per card — a card testing gender, meaning and spelling fails at its weakest member.
Target-language prompt by default — you need production, not just recognition.
An example sentence on every content word, harvested from your own input where possible.
Skip the audio — recorded pronunciations waste card space.
Retire cards of words you now meet constantly in input — real usage has replaced the drill.
config.correction: Audio on everything — it pre-loads the pronunciation loop; images for concrete nouns skip the translation middleman.
config.why: The deck is scaffolding, not the building — its job is to make itself unnecessary.

activities.anchor: met in the wild stick at roughly twice the rate
activities.caption: line up the ninety days
activities.name: f1000BuildOrder

config.prompt: The first 1,000 in ninety days — order the programme:
items: Days 1–30 — pure counts: 20 new cards a day
Days 31–60 — keep 15–20 a day, and harvest every tenth card from your own listening and reading
Days 61–90 — tilt to 50/50 list versus mined, and start testing coverage monthly
Day 90 — roughly 1,200–1,500 words held, unknowns per hundred down from forty-odd to ten or fewer
config.why: There is no trick that beats this budget; there is only a distribution that makes the budget count.
